html:
The Great Law of Peace is the oral constitution that united five nations, the Mohawk, Oneida, Onondaga, Cayuga and Seneca, into the Haudenosaunee Confederacy in what is now New York. Its date is debated, from the 1100s to the 1400s.

Tradition says the Peacemaker and Hiawatha ended cycles of blood feud by persuading the nations to bury their weapons under a great white pine. The law, recorded in wampum belts, set up a Grand Council of chiefs at Onondaga, chosen by clan mothers, who could also remove them.

The Tuscarora joined in the 1720s, making six nations. Benjamin Franklin admired the union, and in 1988 the US Congress recognised its influence on the US Constitution, though historians debate how great it was.
